newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices rise on fresh seasonal demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices rise on fresh seasonal demand.

text.p: Sugar prices rose on Friday on fresh seasonal and bulk consumer demand, traders said.
They said purchases from soft drink producers, coupled with marriage season demand lifted prices up. Limited arrivals kept market sentiment firm, they said.
Ready sugar S-30 rose 15 rupees to 1,315/1,365 per quintal and M-30 gained 30 rupees to 1,375/1,450 per quintal.
Traders said local mills had also been meeting the growing demand from neighbouring states of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.
"The outflow of sugar into other regions has curtailed local supplies," said Shantilal Dedhiya, secretary to the Bombay Sugar Merchants' Association.
Sugar mill delivery rose 10 rupees to 1,265/1,270 per quintal.
"Market setiment is expected to be very firm in the coming weeks as rising summer heat pushes up the demand for soft drinks," Dedhiya said.
